To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the processing of the par- and sympathoinhibitory components of aortic depressor baroreceptor aferents in the Nucleus Tractus Solitarii (Nts) in awake rats is mediated by NMDA and Non NMDA receptors.
processing of the sympatho-inhibitory component of aortic baro-receptor afferent input to the nucleus tractus of solitarii is only partially mediated by non-NMDA and NMDA receptors.
the parasympathomimetic and sympathoinhibitory responses evoked by aortic baroreceptors in the nucleus tract solitarii of awake rats are mediated by both non-NMDA and NMDA receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of aortic barosensitive neurons in the nucleus tract of the solitary tract (NTS) of rats.
the mechanisms of processing of the autonomic components of the aortic baroreflex in awake rats.
the study of the mechanisms of the autonomic responses to baroreceptor aortic stimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processing of afferents from the ADN in the NTS in awake rats is mediated by both ionotropic and metabotropic glutamate receptors.
both components are partially mediated by ionotrophic receptors, but the parasympathomimetic component is mediated to a greater extent than the sympathoinhibiting component.
the afferent baroreceptor input to the nucleus tractus Solitarii is processed by both non-NMDA and NMDA receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the processing of the sympathoexcitatory component is mainly mediated by metabotropic receptors, and that the processing of both parasympathoexcitatory and sympathoinhibitory components is mediated by both ionotropic and metabotropic receptors.

NMDA and kainate receptors are involved in both the parasympathomimetic and sympathoinhibitory components of aortic depressor baroreceptor reflex in the NTS, whereas AMPA receptors are involved in only the parasympatomimetic component.

the processing of the sympathetic component of the NTD baroreceptor aferents is mediated by the ionotropic glutamate receptors, whereas the processing of the paravymathetic component of these aferents seems to be mediated by the ionotrophic as well as the metabotropic glutamate receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NTS afferents from the aortic baroreceptors are not only involved in the regulation of blood pressure, but also in the control of heart rate.
the processing of the sympatho-inhibitory component of aortic baro-receptors in the NTS is partially mediated by NMDA and AMPA receptors.
NMDA receptors in the NTS play a significant role in the processing of the sympathetic component of baroreceptor aferents.
